title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as litho-free capacitor molds
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials, resolving 'taller capacitor vs. costlier etch': sputter ~3 um Al over the storage-node landing pads and let the pad topography seed pore nucleation. Anodizing then grows self-ordered 20-25 nm pores straight down at AR >150:1 in minutes; thin the barrier at the pore bottoms and ALD TiN / high-k / TiN into the pores, keeping the alumina as the mechanical support lattice.
why: Fact 1 and 4: AR ~115-150 without high-AR plasma etch or a capacitor-hole litho layer; ~1.5-2x Cs (or same Cs at ~30% smaller footprint) and removes one of the costliest etch modules.

title: Overlay-free bonded capacitor extension through a sub-pitch nanorod carpet
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation: split the capacitor across two wafers, and split the bond interface into a random carpet of 8 nm TiN-cored, high-k-coated nanorods at 1/4 cell pitch embedded in a common plate. When this wafer is bonded onto the array wafer's isolated storage pads, each pad statistically catches ~10 rod tips while the pad gap (> rod diameter) prevents bridging, so no cell-pitch overlay is needed.
why: Fact 1: adds ~3-5 fF per cell from an independently made wafer (doubling Cs without deeper etch) and decouples capacitor fab from transistor fab (capital, U.S. second source).

title: Dual threshold ladders select one tier, deleting the 3D staircase
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: give each tier's lateral access device two series gates whose thresholds are graded in opposite directions through the stack (front-gate Vt rising with tier number, back-gate Vt falling). Driving the shared vertical front and back gates to the level pair for tier k turns on only tier k (tiers <=k AND >=k), so 8-16 tiers share one contact instead of a staircase.
why: Fact 2 and 7: staircase/contact area grows linearly with tier count; a 16-level ladder cuts staircase area and tier-contact masks ~10x, helping cross the 26-tier break-even.

title: Swiss-roll DRAM: one planar array rolled into forty tiers
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality/curvature: build a single planar 1T1C array (thin trench capacitors) on a strained SiNx/Si bilayer over a sacrificial layer, then release it so the strip self-rolls into a 40-turn tube. All bitlines exit along the strip's leading edge, which stays flat and is hybrid-bonded to a logic die, so 40 effective tiers come from one mask set.
why: Fact 2 and 4: ~40x bits per litho pass without tier-by-tier processing; capital per bit could drop several-fold if roll registration, thermal path and contact yield can be solved.

title: Two-faced wafer: front and back arrays form each differential bitline pair
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: build array plus sense amps on the front, carrier-bond, thin to ~5 um and build a mirror array on the backside at low temperature, joined by nano-TSVs at each sense amp. Each sense amp compares a front bitline with the geometrically identical back bitline, so open-bitline noise mismatch disappears and both faces share one periphery.
why: Fact 7 and resource axis: ~2x bits per wafer start and per quartz-crucible-grown wafer with one set of sense amps; periphery share per bit falls from ~49% toward ~30%.

title: Coaxial cell: capacitor shells wrapped around the vertical transistor pillar
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: in a 4F2 vertical-channel cell, extend the pillar's lower n+ drain upward as a thin outer electrode shell, coat it with high-k, and fill the inter-pillar space with the common plate, while the upper part of the same pillar carries the gate-all-around wordline. Capacitor and transistor live inside one pillar, so there is no storage-node contact or landing-pad layer.
why: Fact 4: 6F2 -> 4F2 (-33% area) and one fewer critical mask; the full pillar sidewall gives ~3-4 fF at AR ~40.

title: Array-only wafers bonded to U.S. mature-node periphery wafers
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: pull all periphery (sense amps, decoders, charge pumps, I/O) off the DRAM wafer onto a 28-40 nm logic wafer from a U.S. foundry, then wafer-to-wafer hybrid bond at ~1 um pitch. The DRAM fab runs only the array flow, so its EUV and high-AR tools spend all their time on bits.
why: Fact 7 and U.S. manufacturability: array efficiency rises from ~51% to ~85% of die area (~1.6x bits per array wafer) and roughly half the process steps move to existing U.S. fabs.

title: Graded-thickness tiers pre-compensate etch taper in deep 3D stacks
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: model the vertical hole's taper before deposition and grade each tier's Si/SiGe (or oxide) thickness so tiers near the narrow bottom are thicker. Lateral channel width and capacitor area then stay matched (Ion and Cs within ~3%) across 100+ tiers from a single etch.
why: Fact 2: ~2x tiers per single-deck etch instead of multi-deck stacking, saving a full deck of masks/etch/alignment per ~64 tiers and tightening the retention tail.

title: Self-aligned dual-workfunction gate tames storage-side GIDL in lateral 3D cells
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: in each lateral 3D access transistor, recess the gate metal laterally from the storage-hole side and refill that ~5 nm edge with a low-workfunction metal, keeping a high-workfunction gate on the bitline side for drive. Field at the storage junction drops and the leakage tail shrinks, with no new mask because the storage hole itself defines the recess.
why: Fact 3: ~10x lower tail leakage -> ~4-8x longer refresh interval, recovering most of the 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth spent on refresh.

title: Clamped-bitline charge-transfer sensing makes bitline capacitance irrelevant
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality: hold each long bitline at a constant potential with a local cascode transistor so the bitline never swings; the cell's charge flows through the cascode into a ~0.5 fF sense node. Signal then scales with Qcell/Csense rather than Qcell/Cbitline.
why: Fact 1 and 7: ~4x more cells per sense amp (less periphery) or ~half the cell capacitance at equal margin; bitline CV2 energy ~5x lower.

title: Grounded shield planes interleaved between tiers to stop row hammer
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: deposit a ~3 nm grounded TiN or doped-Si plane in the dielectric between every pair of 3D tiers (and a buried shield line between adjacent wordlines in 2D). The shields absorb wordline coupling and collect migrating electrons from an aggressor row before they reach victim storage nodes.
why: Fact 9: decouples aggressor and victim, targeting a ~10x higher row-hammer threshold (1k -> 10k+ activations) and less mitigation bandwidth.

title: Overbuild 120 tiers, fuse to 100: tier-level sparing
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial or excessive action: deliberately deposit ~20% more tiers than the product needs, add a per-block tier-remap register, and e-fuse out any tier that fails test (shorts, Vt outliers, weak capacitors). The process window can then be loosened (faster deposition, cheaper precursors) because whole-tier defects become yield-neutral.
why: Fact 2: turns compounding tier loss (0.99^100 ~ 37% yield) into >90% die yield, cutting 3D cost per bit ~2x at a fixed defect density.

title: LC-resonant wordline planes recycle charge in 3D arrays
idea: TRIZ #18 Mechanical vibration (use resonance): 3D wordline planes are large, regular capacitors, so pair each plane group with an on-package RDL inductor and drive it as an LC tank with adiabatic sinusoidal ramps. Most of the ~3 V wordline charge flows back into the tank instead of being dumped to ground every activation.
why: Fact 10: sidesteps the CV2 floor by recovering ~60-80% of wordline energy; activation energy ~30-40% lower.

title: Amplifier tiers interleaved every eight storage tiers
idea: TRIZ #24 Intermediary: every 9th tier of the 3D stack is built from the same lateral transistors but wired as single-ended pre-amplifiers (gated source followers). Each one buffers an 8-tier local vertical bitline segment before it drives the long global bitline to the sense amp below.
why: Fact 1 and 2: cell needs ~1/4 the charge because the local segment capacitance is tiny, so lateral capacitors can be short and thin, making 26+ tiers practical.

title: Chain DRAM: series-connected cells eliminate per-cell bitline contacts
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying (from chain FeRAM and NAND strings): place each access transistor in parallel with its capacitor and chain 8-16 cells in series between a block-select device and the bitline. To read cell k, turn off only its transistor; its capacitor voltage then appears in series on the bitline through the conducting neighbors.
why: Fact 4: planar 4F2-class layout without vertical transistors or buried bitlines and ~8x fewer bitline contacts; ~30% smaller cell at the same F.

title: Smart-Cut donor reuse yields twenty single-crystal tiers per wafer
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: hydrogen-implant one premium 300 mm donor, bond and split a ~50 nm crystalline Si film onto the growing 3D stack, re-polish the donor, and repeat ~20 times so every tier has bulk-quality lateral channels. Bonding at <=400 C builds monolithic crystalline stacks without strained Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy.
why: Fact 2 and resources: single-crystal lateral transistors (a key 3D blocker) without superlattice stress limits; ~20x less crucible-grown Si per tier.

title: Wordline breakers resize the activated row to each request
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: insert a tiny switch transistor every 64 columns along each local wordline (or at each mat of a 3D wordline plane). Column address bits decide how many segments connect, so a 64 B random request opens ~512 bits instead of an 8 KB page while streaming requests still open the full row.
why: Fact 8: activation energy per useful bit falls from ~5.9 pJ toward ~0.5-1 pJ for random access (5-10x), and fewer cells are disturbed (helps row hammer).

title: Antiferroelectric-boundary dielectric biased for a giant effective permittivity
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: tune a ZrO2-rich HfZrO film to sit at its field-induced tetragonal-to-polar transition, and offset the plate voltage so the storage window rides the steep part of the P-E curve. The local dQ/dV gives k_eff ~80-120 without full ferroelectric switching.
why: Fact 1: reaches the k~70 target so a 40:1 capacitor holds what a 75:1 holds today; shorter capacitors shrink 3D tier pitch ~40%.

title: Thermally trimmed wafer distortion for cell-pitch wafer-to-wafer bonding
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: map both wafers' in-plane distortion, then heat the top-wafer bond chuck with a zoned IR array so each region expands by exactly the ppm needed just before contact. Residual overlay falls from ~100 nm to <20 nm, enough to bond a separately built capacitor wafer onto ~40 nm-pitch storage pads.
why: Fact 1 and 4: makes capacitor fab and transistor fab separable (different tools, sites, even companies), each with a simpler, cheaper flow.

title: Wavelength-coded absorber tiers enable stack-first, anneal-later 3D DRAM
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes: give each tier an absorber with a distinct optical resonance (SiGe of graded Ge %, tuned-thickness TiN, plasmonic nanodisks), deposit the whole stack cold, then crystallize or activate each tier's channel with a laser tuned to that tier. Neighboring tiers are transparent at that wavelength and stay cool.
why: Fact 2: removes the thermal-budget conflict of monolithic tiers; one-pass deposition cuts cycle time and capital per tier ~30-50%.

title: Capillary self-alignment for mass-parallel die-to-wafer hybrid bonding
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics and hydraulics: dispense a sub-uL water film on hydrophilic bond sites ringed by hydrophobic borders, drop DRAM dies with a fast coarse pick-and-place, and let surface tension pull each die to <200 nm alignment. Hybrid bonds form as the film evaporates, placing thousands of dies per minute.
why: Fact 6: cuts HBM stacking cost and time, enables finer bond pitch (cheaper TSVs) and known-good-die everywhere; could lift HBM stack yield 10-20 points.

title: Bitlines on the wafer backside for vertical-transistor 4F2 DRAM
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: build vertical transistors and capacitors from the front, then flip, thin and form bitlines from the back so they land directly on pillar bottoms, as backside power delivery does in logic. This replaces the high-resistance buried bitline under the pillars.
why: Fact 4: removes the hardest step of 4F2 vertical-channel DRAM; ~5x lower bitline resistance allows longer bitlines and a 33% smaller cell than 6F2.

title: Plateless bridge capacitor stores one bit between twin nodes
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: merge the two capacitors of a twin cell into one capacitor whose two electrodes are both storage nodes, each reached by its own access transistor on complementary bitlines, with no common plate. Writing puts +V/-V across the single capacitor and the sense amp sees the full differential charge.
why: Fact 1 and 10: ~2x signal per fF lets Cs halve or VARY drop ~30%; deleting the plate layer saves a deposition and contact module.

title: Keep the sacrificial SiGe as hole-storage wells in each tier
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: 3D DRAM flows grow Si/SiGe superlattices and then spend effort removing the SiGe; instead keep a thin SiGe layer under each Si channel as a valence-band quantum well. Holes written by impact ionization or GIDL sit in the well and shift the overlying channel's Vt via body effect, giving a capacitorless 1T cell in every tier.
why: Fact 1 and 2: removes both 3D blockers (capacitor and its lateral integration); ~4F2 per tier and the ~0.2-0.3 eV band offset could extend floating-body retention ~10-100x.

title: Pinned buried-well cells borrowed from image-sensor photodiodes
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying (from CMOS image sensors): store each bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well capped by a p+ pinning layer, the trick that brings photodiode dark current to a few e-/s. A transfer gate dumps the packet onto a floating diffusion and source follower shared by 8 vertically stacked wells, read with correlated double sampling.
why: Fact 3: pinned surfaces cut generation leakage by orders of magnitude, so refresh could move from ms to seconds (refresh energy -90%+); no capacitor and one readout transistor per 8 bits.

title: Vertical CCD columns shift charge through 3D NAND-style gate stacks
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: through a 192-layer deposited (not patterned) gate stack, clock three-phase pulses along a vertical single-crystal channel so charge packets march down the column like a CCD. A base amplifier reads and regenerates every packet on each lap, so refresh is continuous and free.
why: Fact 2 and 4: ~64-192 bits per lithographic hole with no capacitor or per-bit contacts (~10x bits per litho layer); access is serial (~50-100 ns average per 64-position column).

title: Liquid-nitrogen floating-body tiers for a pooled cryogenic memory
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter changes: run a stacked 1T floating-body array at 77 K inside an LN2-immersed rack-level memory pool, where SRH generation and GIDL fall by ~10^6-10^8. Stored hole states then persist for minutes and steeper subthreshold slopes allow ~0.5 V operation.
why: Fact 3 and 10: refresh effectively disappears and CV2 energy falls ~4x; capacitorless ~4F2 cells, provided cooling overhead stays below the energy saved.

title: Inter-tier metal planes double as shared back gates
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: in a stacked thin-Si floating-body array, make the conductive plane between tiers do two jobs: it shields tier from tier and is the negative-biased back gate for both the tier above and the tier below, holding stored holes at the back interface. One deposited film replaces a separate back-gate layer per tier.
why: Fact 1 and 2: double-gate capacitorless cells with no extra back-gate layers; ~10x retention vs single-gate floating body and ~30% thinner tier pitch.

title: Self-latching lateral thyristor in each superlattice tier
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: dope each tier's lateral Si strip in situ as p+/n/p/n+ during epitaxy and gate the p-base with the vertical wordline, so the cell latches itself into a regenerative ON or blocking OFF state. It holds that state on ~pA standby current with no refresh and no capacitor, and reads with a large current ratio.
why: Fact 3 and 8: no refresh (saves 16-33% idle power), non-destructive read (no restore energy), ~6F2 per tier, stackable to 32+ tiers.

title: Goto-pair interband tunneling diodes atop a vertical access transistor
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials: grow two series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunneling diodes directly on top of a 4F2 vertical access transistor. Their negative-differential-resistance curves make the midpoint node bistable, a static latch inside the vertical stack held by a tiny supply current.
why: Fact 3: refresh-free, capacitor-free 4F2 cell with statically held state; access energy ~1/3 of 1T1C because there is no restore cycle.

title: Antiferroelectric gate held between its double loops as volatile bistable
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: use a ZrO2 antiferroelectric layer in each cell transistor's gate and park the wordline plane at a hold bias between the two hysteresis loops, where both the nonpolar and the field-induced polar phase are stable. A short over- or under-pulse toggles the phase and the channel Vt reads it.
why: Fact 1 and 3: capacitorless 1T cell, minor-loop AFE switching aims at >10^12 cycles, no refresh while the hold bias is on, and whole 3D tiers share one gate plane.

title: Nanomechanical gap switch isolates the gain-cell storage gate
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution, used in reverse (field -> mechanics): replace the write transistor of a 2T0C gain cell with an electrostatically actuated vertical NEMS contact switch built in the tier stack. An open air gap has essentially zero leakage, so the read transistor's gate keeps its charge until gate-dielectric leakage alone drains it.
why: Fact 3: refresh interval from ~64 ms to minutes; ~10 ns mechanical write; requires contact endurance near 10^15 (graphene or Ru contacts), which is the main risk.

title: Direct-tunneling hBN floating gate for van der Waals quasi-volatile tiers
idea: TRIZ #21 Skipping (rush through the harmful stage): charge a graphene floating gate through a 3-layer hBN barrier by pure direct tunneling in ns, never entering the Fowler-Nordheim/hot-carrier regime that creates traps. The dangling-bond-free barrier keeps endurance DRAM-like with seconds of retention, and MoS2-channel tiers stack as transferred 2D films.
why: Fact 3: capacitorless 1T cell with ~100x longer retention than DRAM (refresh energy -99%) built in low-temperature tiers stackable on logic.

title: Glass-panel memory sheets on idle display fab lines
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: replace precious 300 mm wafers with cheap Gen-8.5 glass (~5.5 m2) and run 4-8 stacked layers of IGZO 2T0C gain cells at ~1.5 um rules on existing LCD/OLED backplane lines. Panels (~15-20 GB per layer) are diced into memory tiles for a CXL-attached 100-200 ns capacity tier.
why: Capital intensity and cost per bit: reuses depreciated display fabs (no EUV, no quartz crucibles, no Si wafers); target ~$2-5/GB with layer stacking vs ~4x-inflated DRAM contract prices.

title: Inside-out gain cell: storage core gates its surrounding channel tube
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: form each 4F2 pillar as an insulated metal core (the storage node) wrapped by gate oxide and a thin IGZO channel tube that is the read transistor. A small vertical write transistor stacked on top charges the core, so the core gates the whole tube circumference with no separate capacitor.
why: Fact 1 and 4: 2T0C in one 4F2 pillar (vs ~8-12F2 planar gain cells) with ~3x read current per stored charge from the gate-all-around tube.

title: Pillar-word organization: one vertical wordline opens exactly one word
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation: segment the page vertically instead of horizontally. In a 64-tier capacitorless stack, one vertical wordline pillar gates exactly one cell per tier, and each tier has its own short bitline and latch, so one activation delivers a single 64-bit word up the column.
why: Fact 8 and 9: overfetch drops from 128x to ~1x (energy per useful random bit ~5-10x lower) and only 64 cells are disturbed per activation.

title: Merchant pre-grown superlattice starter wafers for capacitorless 3D DRAM
idea: TRIZ #10 Preliminary action: a U.S. epitaxy house pre-grows and sells standardized 64-tier in-situ-doped Si/SiGe superlattice 300 mm wafers with certified defect maps, the way SOI wafers are sold today. Capacitorless 3D cell makers (floating-body, thyristor, gain-cell) start from a finished stack instead of owning epi reactors.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: entrants skip ~$1B of epitaxy capex and months of tier-growth cycle time; creates a new domestic supply-chain node.

title: All-IGZO monolithic memory: n-only periphery in the same tiers
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: build sense amps, decoders and drivers from the same IGZO transistors as the 2T0C array, using bootstrapped n-only (pseudo-CMOS) circuits, so each BEOL tier is a complete memory with no CMOS underneath. The whole stack can sit on any logic die's metal stack.
why: Fact 5 and 7: memory micrometres above compute (~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit vs 3-4 pJ/bit HBM) and periphery needs no separate FEOL; any logic fab's BEOL becomes DRAM capacity.

title: Read floating-body state through the wordline's capacitance, not current
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: keep the bitlines quiet and sense the cell on the wordline instead. Stored body holes change gate-to-channel capacitance (accumulation vs depletion), so a small probe pulse on the vertical wordline couples a state-dependent charge into a wordline-side charge amplifier.
why: Fact 3 and 8: non-destructive, near-zero-current read with no hot-carrier disturb of capacitorless states; read energy ~5x lower.

title: Read-restore 3T gain cell: every read is a refresh
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: add a p-type third transistor whose gate is the precharged read bitline and whose channel links the storage gate to a restore rail. When a stored 1 pulls the read bitline low, the feedback device turns on and tops the storage node back up; a stored 0 leaves the bitline high and the device off.
why: Fact 3: accessed rows refresh themselves, so explicit refresh covers only cold rows (~50-90% fewer refresh operations for typical access patterns); no capacitor.

title: Complementary gain cell: p-WSe2 write tier over n-IGZO read tier
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: make the write transistor p-type (WSe2 or SnO) in one tier and the read transistor n-type IGZO in the tier below, stacked in one footprint. The p-type device passes a full 1 with its wordline at 0 V instead of a ~3 V boost, and its leakage polarity opposes the read device's.
why: Fact 10: removes the wordline boost (~1 V swing, ~9x less wordline CV2) and two-tier stacking halves the planar 2T0C footprint.

title: Bank-switchable floating body: dynamic mode or self-held bipolar latch
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: the same 3D floating-body tiers run in two modes set per bank by source-line bias. At low bias they are dense dynamic cells that need refresh; above the parasitic-BJT latch threshold, impact-ionization feedback holds 1 and 0 statically, so hot banks skip refresh and idle banks drop to near-zero bias.
why: Fact 3: per-bank choice between refresh-free static operation (+10-20% bandwidth) and minimum standby power with no capacitor and no extra transistor.

title: Monolayer MoS2 gain-cell tiers stacked by wafer-scale film transfer
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells and thin films: grow wafer-scale monolayer MoS2 on reusable sapphire templates and transfer the films one by one onto the stack below 300 C, each film becoming a tier of 2T0C cells. The 1.8 eV bandgap and 0.7 nm body give off-currents below ~1e-19 A/um, and with no capacitor the tier pitch can shrink to ~30 nm.
why: Fact 2 and 3: ~3x more tiers per um of stack height than capacitor-based 3D DRAM, retention of hours, no crucible-grown Si per tier.

title: Leakage-ratioed loadless pair holds state across two tiers
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: build a true/complement storage-node pair across two tiers with cross-coupled access devices whose off-state leakage is pre-engineered (Vt, length) to be ~10x stronger toward the rail each node already sits at. Leakage then holds the state like a loadless 4T SRAM instead of erasing it.
why: Fact 3: refresh eliminated (-16-33% idle power, +10-20% bandwidth) at 2x transistor count, but two-tier stacking keeps the footprint near 1T1C; no capacitor.

title: Plane-wide charge-pumping refresh restores millions of cells per pulse
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: instead of read-and-rewrite refresh, apply a periodic gate/source pulse pair to an entire 3D wordline plane. Impact ionization adds holes only in bodies already above a threshold potential (the 1s) while 0s recombine slightly, so every cell on the plane is restored at once without being read.
why: Fact 3: refresh energy and bandwidth fall ~100x because ~10^6 capacitorless cells refresh per pulse with no sense-amp cycles.

title: Negative-capacitance gate stack amplifies tiny gain-cell storage charge
idea: TRIZ #8 Anti-weight: counter the 'weight' of a tiny stored charge with an internal uplift: add a thin ferroelectric layer to the read transistor's gate, matched to operate in its negative-capacitance regime, so the storage node's voltage is amplified at the channel surface. The storage node can then be just the bare gate (~0.1 fF) with an unchanged read margin.
why: Fact 1 and 10: ~2-3x read current per stored electron, storage swing down to ~0.5 V (CV2 -75%) and smaller capacitorless cells.
